correctness.rationale: Exact polar-ray parametrization and Euclidean arclength Jacobian yield first-order normalized mean distance 4/pi*(1+angular mean radial defect) with uniform error O(delta^4 log 1/delta). Direct evaluation of the radial and perimeter integrals gives the stated cubic mesh constant. For regular meshes the singular quadratic chord kernel creates variance/ pi * log(1/alpha), with variance alpha^4/45; high-frequency cancellation excludes a competing angular-density logarithm, giving -pi^2/90. Independent original Euclidean edge-pair quadrature supports both formulas but is not used to prove them.

value.rationale: A nontrivial structural stability law quantifies approach to the unique optimal disk under arbitrary nonuniform inscribed polygonal mesh refinements. Its exact convex cubic energy identifies the meaningful leading mesh design functional, while the sharp regular logarithmic correction captures a singular chord interaction that a naive even-power expansion misses. No exact finite-n optimizer is asserted.
